correctness.rationale: The actual assigned proof diagonalizes the unit complete-graph Laplacian L0=nI−J together with mutually orthogonal rank-one edge projectors P_e=(e_a−e_b)(e_a−e_b)^T/2 for disjoint exceptional edges. Each modified edge has eigenvalue λ_e=n−2+2t_e. Nonexceptional offdiagonals are (1−F(nh))/n>0 and exceptional endpoint entries are 6h Q/[D_n D_λ] with Q=λ[n²−(n−2)λ]h²+12λh+24t, D_s=s²h²+6sh+12. The only possible sign change is the leading coefficient, equivalent to t≤2(n−1)/(n−2) for n≥3. If violated Q has exactly one positive root, giving an eventual negative transition; other exceptional edges do not interfere. F(hL) is positive definite and stochastic, so diagonals remain positive; n=2 handled separately. Independently derived symbolic difference of the exceptional transition and claimed rational formula was identically zero.

value.rationale: A sharp per-edge conductance-tolerance threshold under arbitrarily many noninteracting sparse defects is a natural robust positivity question for network heat integration. Exact no-recovery crossing laws and the independence from other edge weights provide reusable structural information, not merely a test for tiny graphs.

limitations: Only a complete graph with positive conductances and pairwise vertex-disjoint exceptional edges, exact completed [2/2] map; cannot extend to edge-overlap, stages, nonlinear flow or numerical roundoff.
